title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Return True if the tree is a valid binary search tree: for every node, all values in its left subtree are strictly smaller and all values in its right subtree are strictly larger.

hints.1_question: Checking each node against only its parent isn't enough. What range of values is a node allowed to have?
hints.2_nudge: Pass down a lower and upper bound. Going left tightens the upper bound to the parent's value; going right tightens the lower bound.
hints.3_big_hint: ok(n, lo, hi): if lo is not None and n.val <= lo: False; if hi is not None and n.val >= hi: False; return ok(left, lo, n.val) and ok(right, n.val, hi).

known_bugs.name: only compares each node with its direct children
known_bugs.followup: In [5, 4, 6, None, None, 3, 7] the 3 is smaller than its parent 6, but it sits in the right subtree of 5. Do you catch that?

known_bugs.name: allows equal values
known_bugs.followup: Are two equal values allowed in a valid BST according to the statement?

known_bugs.name: uses fixed 32-bit bounds with strict checks
known_bugs.followup: What if a node's value equals one of your starting bounds? Why use None instead of a number?

followups: How does an in-order traversal give an alternative solution?
Why is a plain parent-child comparison insufficient?
